To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we propose a novel stateful data plane API, which can be supported by reusing existing OpenFlow hardware and software, and (ii) we implement a prototype of this API in an open-source platform-independent framework, called OpenState.

(i) stateful OpenFlow applications can be supported by reusing existing OpenFlow hardware primitives, and (ii) stateful applications are more expressive than stateless ones, and therefore, they are more suitable to be deployed inside the switches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a platform-independent stateful programming API for switches, which we call OpenState, that can be used to implement a wide range of network applications.
the development of a platform-agnostic, stateful, and performant data plane programming API, which can be deployed in OpenFlow switches, as well as in programmable switches from other vendors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed API can be implemented in OpenFlow switches, and it is a step towards the vision of stateful programmable switches, with no need of additional hardware.
OpenFlow switches can be programmed in a stateful way, without requiring to resort to closed platforms.

OpenState is a viable alternative programming abstraction for the data plane, which is platform independent, and can be efficiently implemented in current OpenFlow switches, and that it is a promising candidate for the programmable data plane of the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OpenState is an OpenFlow extension that enables stateful data plane applications to be written in a vendor-agnostic way, and deployed inside the switch.
we propose a new stateful table-based API (OpenState), and that we show how it is supported by (mostly reusing core primitives) in OpenFlow devices, which is a proof of concept of our proposal.

we have devised and implemented the first platform-independent stateful data plane abstraction for OpenFlow switches, which can be used to program stateful network applications in a platform-independent fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while OpenFlow is a great first step, it is still a long way from enabling the deployment of complex network applications in the switch.
, by exploiting existing OpenFlow primitives, we can extend the match/action abstraction with stateful behavior without requiring any modification to the OpenFlow protocol.

, in order to achieve a stateful programmable data plane, we do not need to start from scratch, and we do not need a new programming language, but we can rely on a well-known formalism (extended finite state machines) and on the already existing OpenFlow infrastructure.
